Not examined: dependency vulnerability scanning (requires external tools), remote OAuth provider testing, TLS configuration audit.

dropped.label: Potential CSRF in OAuth flow
dropped.reason: State parameter is properly validated before being used. Code at handlers/auth.go lines 66-70 validates that the state from the query parameter matches the session state before processing.

findings.title: Missing SameSite cookie attribute in default configuration
findings.evidence: Line 40 of .defaults.yml shows sameSite is commented out. When not configured, pkg/cookie/cookie.go line 183 defaults to http.SameSite(0), which sends no SameSite attribute to the browser.
findings.impact: Without an explicit SameSite attribute, cookies are vulnerable to Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) attacks. While modern browsers (Chrome 80+, Firefox 69+) default to 'Lax' mode when SameSite is missing, older browsers and clients do not enforce this protection. A malicious website could trigger requests that include the VouchCookie.
findings.preconditions: User is authenticated with VouchCookie set. User visits a malicious website that attempts to make a cross-site request to vouch-proxy (e.g., to the /validate endpoint or other sensitive endpoints).
findings.recommendation: Set a default value for the sameSite cookie attribute in .defaults.yml. Use 'lax' or 'strict' depending on use case. Example: Change line 40 from '# sameSite:' to 'sameSite: lax'
findings.verification: After setting sameSite in configuration, verify that the Set-Cookie response header includes 'SameSite=Lax' or 'SameSite=Strict' by examining HTTP responses from the /login endpoint.

triage.reason: No compensating control enforces CSRF protection at a higher layer
The SameSite value is controlled by configuration, not attacker-controlled, but the default configuration is missing this security setting
Cookies without SameSite attribute are vulnerable by design in older browsers
The lack of SameSite attribute is in the shipped default configuration
Authentication cookies have high security value
No external control documented that sets SameSite by default
This is not a defense-in-depth issue; it's a primary protection that should be in place

findings.limits: This finding addresses the default configuration only. The application can still be configured securely by setting sameSite in the configuration file. The actual exploitability depends on browser version and specific deployment configuration.

ruled_out.where: golang-jwt/jwt v5.3.1 used with RegisteredClaims, which validates expiration by default. No SkipClaimsValidation flag is used in ParseTokenString (pkg/jwtmanager/jwtmanager.go line 150-157).

getValidRequestedURL (handlers/login.go lines 199-246) validates requested URLs against configured domains and checks for dangerous prefixes (line 115: badStrings array with https://, http://, data:, etc.)
State parameter is securely generated (handlers/login.go line 290: securerandom.URLBase64InBytes) and validated on auth callback (handlers/auth.go line 67: session.Values["state"] != queryState)
